BetaNYC visits each source's website and records what it finds. A copy ships in the package (data/ny-data-portal-registry.json); when the server starts it checks BetaNYC's published copy for a newer one and keeps it in a cache on your computer. check_source makes one request to a portal's web page when asked and compares the answer with the registry row.

Changed by BetaNYC: The registry is BetaNYC's own work, checked by hand. This server adds to each row an id, a platform family from a hand-made table (data/platform-families.json), and the place it covers, from a hand-made list of New York's counties, cities, boroughs and regions (data/ny-places.json).

dataset.scopeNote: Known gap: Rows marked not yet confirmed need a person to check them before you rely on them. Known gap: The place list (data/ny-places.json) was written by hand and has not been checked against an official gazetteer; a city that spans counties is listed under its main county. Caveat: Endpoints are copied from the registry, never guessed. Rows marked undocumented use an API the owner has not published, which may change. Caveat: check_source reports one page request at the moment you ask; a portal that blocks automated requests is reported as blocked, not worked around.

provenance: Official source: yes. This data is BetaNYC's, derived from it, not an official New York State, New York City and other New York governments record.

BetaNYC's harvester reads each portal's catalog through the Socrata Discovery API (Socrata is now the Data and Insights division of Tyler Technologies, per dev.socrata.com), read-only, and builds an index file. The index is published as a GitHub release, and the server downloads it on first run into a cache on your computer. Answers come from that file, with no request to the portals.

Changed by BetaNYC: Only datasets, maps, files and links are kept. Each dataset is joined to its registry row (place, platform family, portal), and gets download links worked out from Socrata's documented endpoints. find_joinable labels columns as join keys (such as BBL or census tract) from BetaNYC's hand-made table of column names (data/key-columns.json).

dataset.scopeNote: Known gap: Only portals in the registry that run Socrata. Datasets added after the last harvest are missing until the index is rebuilt. Caveat: This is a catalog of datasets, not the data. Every dataset row links to its page on its own portal: check a dataset's details there. Caveat: To report an error in a dataset or its description, use the contact on that dataset's own portal page (Socrata pages have Contact Dataset Owner). Caveat: whats_new compares harvests of this index; a dataset is new to the index, which may not be the day the portal published it. Caveat: An empty answer means not in this index, not that the data does not exist.

provenance: Official source: yes. This data is BetaNYC's, derived from it, not an official New York State, New York City and other New York governments record.

BetaNYC's harvester reads each portal's public catalog (its Hub feed or its portal search, and each layer's field list), read-only and spaced out as each site's robots.txt asks, and builds an index file. The index is published as a GitHub release, and the server downloads it on first run into a cache on your computer. Answers come from that file, with no request to the portals.

Changed by BetaNYC: Esri's own national layers and items owned by other organizations are left out, as are portals that block automated clients. Each dataset is joined to its registry row (place, platform family, portal). find_joinable labels columns as join keys from BetaNYC's hand-made table of column names (data/key-columns.json).
